title: Sequence-Length-Aware Kernel Selection Guidelines
author: Priya Desai
content:
Summary:

This document defines runtime and compile-time guidelines for selecting and shipping GPU kernels that are aware of sequence-length distributions for inference workloads. The intention is to reduce average token latency and per-token cost while preserving memory safety and predictable tail latencies for Redwood's serving runtime.

Audience:
- Serving runtime engineers
- Kernel authors and compiler integrators
- Capacity and SRE teams responsible for GPU fleet allocation
- Model onboarding engineers

Motivation:
- Customer workloads vary widely in sequence length: short chat turns, medium-length instruction completions, and long context retrievals. One-size-fits-all kernels yield suboptimal latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Kernel selection decisions influence L2 (memory) usage, register pressure, occupancy, and cache behavior. These directly impact SLO attainment and unit economics.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a deterministic policy for picking kernels based on observed per-tenant sequence-length histograms and SLOs.
  - Standardize telemetry and sampling to make kernel decisions auditable and rollouts reversible.
  - Ensure safe fallbacks when kernel selection fails or a kernel binary is missing.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a comprehensive compiler design document; it focuses on serving-level selection and operational policies.

Definitions:
- hot-path kernel: highly optimized kernel tuned for short sequences and low-latency, potentially at higher per-token compute cost.
- bulk kernel: throughput-optimized kernel that achieves better utilization for long sequences by amortizing setup overhead.
- shard-compile: precompiled binary targeted at a specific GPU architecture and sequence-length profile.

Telemetry and signals to collect (minimum required):
1) Sequence-length histogram per customer and per route (bucketed: 0-32,33-128,129-512,513-2048,>2048).
2) P50/P95/P99 generation latency broken down by sequence-length bucket and kernel_variant.
3) GPU occupancy, register usage, and SM utilization per kernel_variant.
4) Memory allocations and peak GPU memory per request.
5) Kernel failure counts, fallback invocations, and compile-time errors.

Policy: Kernel selection priority
1) Hard SLO routes (SLO target <= 100ms P95): use hot-path kernels for any bucket with median length <= 128 tokens.
2) Cost-sensitive routes (billing tier flagged as cost_aware): prefer bulk kernels for median length > 256 tokens unless P95 tail is breached.
3) Mixed workloads: use dynamic split routing — short sequences map to hot-path containers, long sequences map to bulk containers.

Configuration table (example):
| config_key | description | default | allowed_values | owner |
|-----------|-------------|---------|----------------|-------|
| kernel.selection.mode | Global selection mode | mixed | mixed|hot-only|cost-only | Runtime Platform Team |
| kernel.bucket_thresholds | Buckets used for histograms | 32,128,512,2048 | comma-separated ints | Serving Runtime |
| kernel.rollout.canary_pct | Percent of traffic to try new kernel | 1 | 0-50 | Runtime Platform Team |
| kernel.fallback_on_failure | Whether to fallback to reference kernel | true | true|false | Runtime Platform Team |

Selection algorithm (high-level pseudocode):

1) Periodic profiler job (freq: 10m) computes per-route histogram and cost/latency delta between variants.
2) If median_length <= short_threshold and (P95_hot <= SLO or cost delta < cost_threshold), set kernel_variant=hot for that route.
3) Else if median_length > long_threshold and bulk_variant P50 cost < hot_variant P50 cost by 10%, set kernel_variant=bulk.
4) For mixed buckets where a single variant cannot meet SLO, configure split routing: route short tokens to hot and long tokens to bulk using request-length header.

Example YAML configuration (runtime):

kernel_selection:
  mode: mixed
  short_threshold: 128
  long_threshold: 256
  buckets: [32, 128, 512, 2048]
  fallback_on_failure: true
  canary:
    enabled: true
    percent: 1

Operational runbook (short):
1) On performance regression alert (route P95 breach):
   a) Check kernel failure counts and recent kernel rollouts.
   b) If a new kernel binary was deployed in the last 60m, immediately route 100% of that route to fallback variant and mark the new kernel rollout as paused.
   c) Collect last 1 hour of sequence-length histogram and kernel-level telemetry.
   d) If telemetry indicates memory-unbounded growth, escalate to Kernel SIG and open an incident.
2) If tail latency is high but kernel failure counts are low:
   a) Consider enabling split routing and increasing hot-path capacity.
   b) If cost budget allows, temporarily prefer hot-path for affected customers with strict SLOs.

Kernel binary and compatibility matrix (textual):
- Each kernel build must be annotated with: supported_arch (e.g., ampere, h100), max_sequence_optimized, workspace_bytes_required, and ABI version.
- The runtime will refuse to load a kernel whose ABI version does not match the runtime ABI.
- Compatibility policy: minor ABI mismatches can be allowed under a feature-flag after a canary period. Major ABI mismatches require a compatibility release and coordination with SRE.

Security and safety considerations:
- Kernel binaries are signed and verified at load time. Unsigned kernels must be rejected.
- All kernel selection decisions and sample inputs used during canaries must be logged with redaction for PII.
- For private deployments (customer-managed), provide a checker utility that validates kernel signatures and workspace guarantees before enabling runtime opt-in.

Rollout and testing guidance:
- Preflight tests for a kernel must include: microbenchmarks across bucketed sequence lengths, memory-pressure stress tests, and a synthetic tail-latency workload.
- Canary: default 1% of traffic for 30 minutes, monitor P99, error rate, and memory spikes. Abort criteria: >20% increase in P99 or any OOM in canary hosts.
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with health check windows of 30 minutes per step.

Kernel authors checklist (before upload):
- [ ] Provide per-bucket latency and memory table for supported sequence lengths.
- [ ] Attach signed artifact with ABI metadata and compile flags.
- [ ] Add unit and integration tests covering boundary buckets (e.g., 31/32, 128/129).
- [ ] Provide expected GPU occupancy and register pressure metrics.

Metrics and dashboards to create:
- Per-route kernel_variant P50/P95/P99 latency heatmap keyed by sequence-length bucket.
- Kernel failure and fallback rate per hour.
- Kernel memory headroom gauge: (allocated_workspace / total_gpu_memory).
- Cost per million tokens by kernel_variant.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Serving Runtime Team (owners: @serving-runtime).
- Kernel SIG: cross-team working group (runtime, compiler, perf, SRE).
- Escalation steps: page-on-call -> Kernel SIG -> Eng Infra Director.

FAQ (selected):
Q: How do we handle models with extreme variable-length behavior (chat + docs embeddings)?
A: Use split routing with an upfront classifier that routes high-context requests to bulk pools and short-turn chat to hot pools. If a classifier is not available, default to conservative bulk which preserves throughput.

Q: What if a kernel optimizes a single bucket but regresses others?
A: Reject that kernel for default rollout. Kernels should provide a performance matrix and only opt-in for specific routes via explicit canary-based policy.

Appendix: sample CLI commands
- Compile shard for Ampere with optimizations:
  $ kernel-cli build --arch ampere --max-seq 512 --optimize=short-path --output kernel_ampere_s512.bin

- Validate kernel before upload:
  $ kernel-cli validate kernel_ampere_s512.bin --check-abi --check-signature --report ./reports/s512.json
